issues.description: The problem specification and the template expect a public Farm.singFarmSong() method, but the provided solution exposes a public playFarmSong() method instead. This name/signature mismatch (singFarmSong vs playFarmSong) is a structural API difference that will confuse students and break any code/tests that call singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the method name consistent. Either rename the solution's playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to playFarmSong(). Also update any references (e.g., Main and tests) to use the same method name.

issues.description: The UML and solution define a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal), but the template's singFarmSongVerse method signature omits the Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out). This prevents students from implementing the verse method with the intended signature and will cause a structural mismatch when integrating with the solution approach.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the parameter in the template method signature: change private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This aligns the template with the UML and the solution, and lets students implement the verse logic correctly.

issues.description: The public method that plays the farm song is named singFarmSong() in the problem statement and the template, but the solution implementation names the method playFarmSong(). This is the same conceptual operation (play the Old MacDonald song for all animals) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students mapping the requirement to the reference solution (and causes the commented Main example to reference a non-existent method name in the solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a singFarmSong() wrapper that delegates to playFarmSong(), and update any example usage (e.g., Main) to match. This aligns the solution with the problem statement and template and removes the naming mismatch.
